production_defect_evidence: execute_once.py:288 now calls registration_schema.validate_identity(reg); the R1 hardcoded d2_retained276_continuation_registration_v1 guard is gone. findings.summary: AUD_SHA pin does not match the on-disk auditor it guards.
findings.detail: wrapper.py:33 pins AUD_SHA = 884cf86a3b044c8664873221505d6e64022a1303ed067116174c585682760285. The file it loads, wrapper.py:32 AUD_PATH = OUT/audit_candidates.py, hashes to 604133a1b3dc34616cee2401662c573662c9475363d2c2e0254aeffa2094bcb7. freeze-hashes.json:55 records that same 604133 value, so the disk file and freeze manifest agree and the wrapper pin is the stale value. load_auditor (wrapper.py:103-106) fails closed with 'Auditor source digest differs'. run_audit (wrapper.py:226) and the pins-unchanged gate (wrapper.py:245) use the same pin.
findings.failure_scenario: Any invocation of wrapper.py run_audit or full_mode (wrapper.py:217, 274) raises before the audit runs.
findings.consequence: Post-run audit is blocked. Fail-closed, so no bypass and no false pass. Grep shows execute_once.py does not call the wrapper audit path, so the launch path itself is not shown to be blocked; the parent should confirm this.
findings.fix: Repin AUD_SHA to 604133a1b3dc34616cee2401662c573662c9475363d2c2e0254aeffa2094bcb7 only after the separate six-candidate auditor rebind the brief requires, or make the rebind the owner of that value.

findings.summary: The one-use launch marker is written before the registration digest is verified.
findings.detail: execute() validates identity (line 288), mkdirs the output (line 290), and saves launch-marker.json (lines 291-292). Only then does load_registration (line 313, which checks sha(path)==expected_sha at runner.py:362) run. A call with a valid-shape registration and a wrong registration_sha therefore consumes the single-use marker and launches nothing. R1 also recorded marker consumption as a failure mode.
findings.failure_scenario: execute(valid_v2_registration, wrong_sha) writes launch-marker.json, then raises 'External registration digest differs'. A later correct call sees the marker already present.
findings.consequence: A caller error burns the one-use marker before any worker starts. Documented in the code comment as intended ('exclusive marker precedes verified registration loading'), so this is a design choice, not a bypass. Flagged because it repeats the R1 consumption symptom.
findings.fix: Optional: verify the registration digest before the marker write, or record the failure separately. Parent decides.

findings.summary: ROOT in the boundary regression is computed one directory too high and is unused.
findings.detail: The file is at learning/runs/v2/<prep>/; parents[3] is the repo root and parents[4] is its parent. ROOT is never referenced in the file. Dead code, not a correctness failure.
findings.failure_scenario: None at runtime; a future use of ROOT would resolve outside the repo.
findings.consequence: Cosmetic, but misleading for a regression file that is meant to be exact.

findings.summary: registration_schema is imported before its pin is verified.
findings.detail: execute_once.py:18 and runner.py:21 import registration_schema from the script directory at module load. The registration pins registration_schema.py (f8956515...), and that matches disk, but verify_pins runs later inside load_registration (runner.py:363). A modified registration_schema.py would execute before the pin check.
findings.failure_scenario: A tampered registration_schema.py in the frozen prep directory runs its module body before any pin check.
findings.consequence: Trust in the shared schema module rests on directory freeze, the same trust the launcher and runner already place in their own source. Not a new bypass; noted for completeness.
findings.fix: Optional: verify the module hash in the wrapper before launch, or accept the existing freeze model.

findings.summary: Boundary regression covers only the execute() entry; the runner-side identity rejection has no test.
findings.detail: The test exercises execute_once.execute with reached and rejected cases. runner.validate_registration calls the same validate_identity (runner.py:125ish) but no test drives it with the wrong schema, run_id, or output.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit that removes the runner's validate_identity call would not be caught by this test.
findings.consequence: Coverage gap for the second entry point the brief names.
findings.fix: Add a runner.validate_registration rejection case to the same regression file.

findings.summary: Auditor drops the PYTHONPATH-unset check and one Entry Adam mutation test relative to R1.
findings.detail: R1 audit_candidates.py:127 had check('PYTHONPATH' not in os.environ). R2 removes it. R1 test_audit_candidates.py:139-140 had the Entry Adam mutation test; R2 removes it. The brief says the embedded auditor is inactive until a separate six-candidate rebind, so this is informational. test_audit_candidates.py in R2 is pinned in freeze-hashes.json.
findings.failure_scenario: None for the launch path. The auditor's environment check is weaker in R2.
findings.consequence: Informational. Rebind should decide whether the check and test return.
findings.fix: Restore the removed check and test in the rebind, or record why they were dropped.
